modelAsset.title: Bald eagle · revised body, plumage and flight
modelAsset.author: Pigcraft (https://sketchfab.com/s8819296); body, materials, feet and rig revisions by PhenoVoxel Archive
modelAsset.surfaceType: Revised Pigcraft flight mesh and separate revised Grab3D standing mesh
modelAsset.changes: Fuller standing breast and shoulders, lifted folded tail, remodeled four-toed feet and talons, and softer matte feather detail. The flight mesh has a broader inner wing, a revised flight silhouette, and articulated tucked feet.
modelAsset.biology: Mature adult traits. Shape and contact are educational reconstructions. Cadence is referenced to a preliminary field sample, with authored joint angles and scene motion.

viewerRig.type: Two credited adult exteriors, 11-control flight skeleton and standing neck rig
viewerRig.scope: Ground contact, flapping, glide and shallow bank. The 2.53 Hz cadence uses a preliminary field estimate. Forces, speed, individual geometry and joint trajectories are uncalibrated.
viewerRig.description: Folded wings and four planted digits per foot in standing. Broad articulated wings and tucked feet in flight.

modelAsset.retainedUVScope: Existing feather and eye source coordinates retained on surviving geometry. Newly modeled feet and talons use vertex pigment.

behaviors.label: Fly
behaviors.description: Two short flapping bouts alternate with broad-wing coasting. The paired wings lift together and the wrists flex back on the upstroke. Both feet stay tucked. Active beats use the 2.53 Hz mean reported in a preliminary field sample of six bald eagles.
behaviors.evidence: Bergen et al. distinguish flapping and gliding in free flight. Lanzone et al. report speed of the active wingbeat in a conference abstract.
behaviors.timeScale: Active cadence 2.53 Hz in the reference sample. Display phase lengths and translation are authored.

rendering.reason: Rhythm is referenced to a field sample. Joint paths, travel speed and aerodynamic forces are illustrative.

behaviors.studyNote: Pause at the raised and lowered wings or between bouts. Active cadence uses a six-bird preliminary field estimate.

behaviors.label: Glide
behaviors.description: The adult moves forward in a shallow descent with broad, nearly level wings. The separated outer primaries remain spread and the feet stay against the underside.
behaviors.evidence: Adult flight photographs and free-flight observations of gliding descent.

rendering.reason: Qualitative unpowered glide. Descent angle, airspeed and lift remain uncalibrated.

behaviors.studyNote: The held wings distinguish the glide from the active wingbeat study. The shallow descent uses display units.

behaviors.label: Bank and return
behaviors.description: A shallow bank to either side returns to level wings. Small changes in wing elevation and tail angle are shown with the feet tucked.
behaviors.evidence: Illustrative wing and tail posture during an already airborne bank.
behaviors.timeScale: uncalibrated illustrative display seconds; no biological clock

rendering.reason: Body roll and trim are authored. Turn radius, forces and trajectory are uncalibrated.

behaviors.label: Standing
behaviors.description: Both feet are planted on a flat reference surface. Each foot has three forward toes and a rear hallux. The folded wings cover the flanks, while the compact tail clears the support.
behaviors.evidence: Adult standing documented by USFWS. Digit arrangement and relative curvature informed by raptor morphology.

rendering.reason: Two-foot contact is built into the pose. Balance forces and gripping are outside this study.

behaviors.label: Standing head turns
behaviors.description: A fixed, two-foot standing posture with small upper-neck and head turns to alternate sides and back to center.
behaviors.evidence: Primary head-position observations; authored exterior articulation
behaviors.timeScale: Eight-second illustrative viewing interval; uncalibrated behavioral timing

rendering.reason: Head position illustrates sideways looking. Turning angles and gaze are unmeasured.

sources.title: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service · Bald Eagle
sources.scope: Adult plumage and observations of standing on rocks and ground, perching and soaring.

sources.title: Fowler, Freedman & Scannella (2009) · Raptor talon morphology
sources.scope: Digit orientation and relative talon geometry. Bald eagle outer digits also bear well-developed curved talons.

sources.title: Lanzone et al. (2017) · Eagle telemetry and accelerometry, conference abstract
sources.scope: Preliminary field sample of six bald eagles, mean active cadence 2.53 Hz (SE 0.03). It does not establish joint paths, stroke angles or the duration of model phases.

sources.title: Watts & Markham (2023) · Bald eagle size in the Chesapeake Bay
sources.scope: Regional museum measurements of wing chord, primary length, tarsus, hallux, tail and bill. Adult proportions vary among individuals and sexes.

anatomy.name: Adult head, bill and eye
anatomy.description: A mature adult has a white head, pale eye with a pronounced brow, and a hooked yellow bill. Facial relief follows the credited source.

anatomy.name: Feet and talons
anatomy.description: The lower tarsus is bare and scuted. Three toes point forward and the hallux points back. Dark, recurved talons are individually shaped, with large inner and hind claws and substantial outer claws.

anatomy.name: Flight feathers and white tail
anatomy.description: Dark layered coverts and flight feathers surround a contrasting white tail. Broad inner wings and separated outer primary tips define the glide. The feather movement follows the arm and wrist controls.

review.status: Species-referenced exterior and finite motion studies. Independent validation pending.
review.movementStudyScope: Two-foot standing contact, preliminary telemetry cadence, flapping and passive glide. Illustrative joint paths and normalized travel.
